paper.title: Excellent mechanical properties and underlined deformation twinning mechanism of a low-carbon low-density cryogenic steel
paper.paper_scope: Mechanical properties, deformation microstructures and the deformation-twinning mechanism of a single low-carbon low-density austenite-based duplex steel Fe-35Mn-6Al-0.1C (wt.%) are studied under room temperature (RT) and liquid nitrogen temperature (LNT) via tensile and instrumented Charpy V-notch impact testing, with SFE/thermodynamic and flow-stress modelling.

alloys.description: Low-carbon low-density cryogenic steel designed and fabricated in this study; an austenite (FCC γ)-based duplex structure with a small fraction (~3 vol.%) of BCC α ferrite, designed for excellent cryogenic toughness and ductility via 35%Mn, 6%Al and 0.1%C alloying.
alloys.alloys_notes: Measured composition by wet-chemical analysis (wt.%, Table 1): Mn 35.14, Al 5.97, C 0.095, Nb 0.11, V 0.10, Mo 1.24, W 0.95, Fe Bal.; austenite (γ) fraction ~97 vol.% and α ferrite ~3 vol.%; measured density 7.18 g·cm⁻³; calculated SFE γ_SFE = 62.64 mJ·m⁻² (RT) and 49.46 mJ·m⁻² (LNT); after electrolytic extraction V fully dissolved while ~0.047 wt.% Nb, 0.017 wt.% Mo and 0.024 wt.% W exist in MC carbide.

source.reason: The paper designs and studies exactly one low-carbon low-density steel with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-6Al-0.1C-0.1Nb-0.1V-1Mo-1W (wt.%), repeatedly referred to as Fe35Mn6Al0.1C / Fe-35Mn-6Al-0.1C; since only one composition system is investigated, a single alloy entity is defined.

processes.description: Hot-rolled rods solution-treated at 1050 °C for 2 h followed by oil quenching to obtain an equiaxed grain structure (mean γ grain size ~10.8 μm, ~3 vol.% α, weak texture).
processes.processes_notes: Precursor condition for both tensile and impact testing; the ingot was homogenized at 1150 °C for 4 h and hot-rolled to 16.5 mm rods before solution treatment. The text describes the quench inconsistently as 'oil quenching' (b0015) and the tensile specimens as 'water quenched' (b0026).

source.reason: This is the single starting/heat-treatment condition applied to the steel before testing: 'solution-treated at 1050 °C for 2 h followed by oil quenching' (b0015), with the initial microstructure characterized in section 3.1.

processes.description: Uniaxial tensile testing at room temperature (20 °C) at an initial strain rate of 1.0×10⁻³ s⁻¹, with interrupted tests at engineering strains of 3, 10, 20, 28, 38 and 55 %; deformed microstructure controlled by dislocation substructure refinement with twinning only just before necking.
processes.processes_notes: Shares the solution-treated precursor with the LNT tensile state; interrupted specimens at multiple strains belong to this same terminal deformation state.

source.reason: The paper defines a distinct RT deformation state: tensile deformed at room temperature, labeled RT, examined by EBSD/TEM and reported with RT mechanical properties; RT is one of the two deformation temperatures that structure the study.

processes.process_name: tensile deformation at liquid nitrogen temperature
processes.description: Uniaxial tensile testing at liquid nitrogen temperature (−196 °C) at an initial strain rate of 1.0×10⁻³ s⁻¹, with interrupted tests at engineering strains of 3, 10, 20, 28, 38 and 55 %; deformation controlled by dislocation substructure refinement plus twinning nucleated just after yielding.
processes.processes_notes: Shares the solution-treated precursor with the RT tensile state; LNT is the second deformation temperature structuring the study and gives the four-stage hardening behavior.

source.reason: The paper defines a distinct LNT deformation state: tensile deformed at liquid nitrogen temperature, labeled LNT, examined by EBSD/TEM/XRD and reported with LNT mechanical properties.

processes.processes_notes: Shares the solution-treated precursor; impact deformation state distinguished from the tensile deformation states and from the LNT impact state.

The Fe-35Mn-6Al-0.1C alloy in its solution-treated (1050 °C/2 h + oil quench) condition is the reference material whose initial microstructure (phase map, KAM, IPF, SAD patterns) is characterized in section 3.1.
The Fe-35Mn-6Al-0.1C alloy tensile deformed at room temperature, with distinct mechanical properties (YS 251 MPa, UTS 580 MPa, TEL 52 %) and deformation microstructure reported for RT.
The Fe-35Mn-6Al-0.1C alloy tensile deformed at liquid nitrogen temperature, with distinct mechanical properties (YS 497 MPa, UTS 945 MPa, TEL 75.5 %) and deformation microstructure reported for LNT.
The Fe-35Mn-6Al-0.1C alloy after Charpy V-notch impact at room temperature, characterized by its fracture morphology and near-fracture microstructure (Fig. 9(a–e)), impact energy 331±4 J.
The Fe-35Mn-6Al-0.1C alloy after Charpy V-notch impact at liquid nitrogen temperature, characterized by its fracture morphology and near-fracture microstructure (Fig. 9(f–j)), impact energy 254±6 J.

unmapped_findings: The designed steel has high stacking fault energy (γ_SFE = 62.64 mJ·m⁻² at RT and 49.46 mJ·m⁻² at LNT) yet still develops deformation twins at both temperatures, which is attributed to stress concentration induced by a planar dislocation substructure and short-range ordering (L1₂-type SRO).
Measured density of the investigated steel (Archimedes principle) is 7.18 g·cm⁻³.
Austenite is highly stable: XRD and Thermo-Calc phase diagram show ~97 vol.% austenite plus ~3 vol.% BCC α phase with no strain-induced martensitic transformation even at LNT.
Experimental critical twinning stresses were ~723 MPa at RT and ~778 MPa at LNT, lower than most model predictions; deformation twinning started at ~28 % tensile strain at RT but at ~10 % at LNT.
